speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were taking and when you started noticing the rash and joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the joints swollen and warm to the touch, and do you have any swelling in your hands or feet? Have you noticed any blood in your urine or any abdominal pain?

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any abdominal pain or notice changes in your urine color, such as it appearing pink or red? I would like to request a urinalysis to check for blood or protein. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

text: The normal urinalysis makes Henoch-Schönlein purpura less likely. Given the timing after amoxicillin, could this be a serum sickness-like reaction? I will check for any signs of angioedema or respiratory distress. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diagnosed with acute sinusitis one week ago, no known history of adverse drug reactions, immunizations up to date. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: The images show a morbilliform rash on the trunk and extremities with no signs of angioedema. Given the timing after amoxicillin and the absence of renal involvement, this is likely a drug eruption. DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced morbilliform drug eruption
